strings.name: Tan Su Shan
strings.summary: Tan Su Shan worked in trading and private banking at international banks before joining DBS in 2010. She led wealth management, consumer banking and institutional banking before becoming its first female CEO in 2025. She also supports women's careers in finance and participates in public affairs.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026. Succession announcements are distinguished from appointments taking effect, and group offices from subsidiary roles. Oxford MA follows the official designation, without implying a research master's degree. Birth date awaits verification.
strings.influence.rationale: Developed wealth management and institutional banking at DBS, becoming an important leader in Singapore's financial sector.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Studied Politics, Philosophy and Economics at Lincoln College, Oxford; her official biography lists an MA. Executive courses at Harvard, Stanford and elsewhere are not an MBA.
strings.facts.f2.label: Public service
strings.facts.f2.value: Served as a Nominated Member of Singapore's Parliament from 2012 to 2014, rather than holding an elected seat.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Leadership across banking businesses
strings.highlights.h1.text: Progressed from wealth management and consumer banking to institutional banking and then group CEO.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Network for women in finance
strings.highlights.h2.text: Founded the Financial Women's Association Singapore in 2001 as its founding president, supporting professional connections and mentoring.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Attends third-quarter results briefing
strings.timeline.t1.text: Discussed markets trading income, AI and operational resilience; group quarterly net profit was SGD2.81 billion, down 5% year on year.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Becomes DBS Hong Kong vice chairman
strings.timeline.t2.text: Appointed director and vice chairman of the Hong Kong subsidiary, not chairman of the group.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Becomes group CEO and director
strings.timeline.t3.text: Succeeded Piyush Gupta, becoming DBS's first female CEO.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Appointed deputy CEO and named successor
strings.timeline.t4.text: Continued leading institutional banking while becoming deputy CEO; the group CEO transition followed the next year.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Begins Indonesian subsidiary oversight role
strings.timeline.t5.text: Became President Commissioner of PT Bank DBS Indonesia, a role held until 2024.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes a Nominated Member of Parliament
strings.timeline.t6.text: Began serving as a Nominated Member of Singapore's Parliament, with her term ending in 2014.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joins DBS
strings.timeline.t7.text: Moved from international banking to DBS, initially concentrating on building wealth management.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Founds Financial Women's Association
strings.timeline.t8.text: Established a nonprofit supporting professional connections and development for women in Singapore's financial industry.
